props.title: John Wick
props.initialSlug: Retired hitman seeks revenge for his murdered dog.

sections.content: **John Wick (2014)** (2014) revolutionized modern action cinema with its "gun-fu" choreography and neon-noir style. Director Chad Stahelski, a former stunt coordinator, brought raw authenticity to the fight scenes by letting Keanu Reeves perform extended takes without quick cuts - a stark contrast to the shaky-cam style popularized by **The Bourne Identity** (2002). The film established a new gold standard for action choreography, influencing works like **Atomic Blonde** (2017) and **Nobody** (2021). Its world-building of The Continental hotel and its assassin underworld created a unique mythology that elevated it beyond typical revenge plots.

sections.content: The franchise's influence extends beyond action choreography. Its stylized production design, particularly the neon-saturated cinematography by Jonathan Sela, sparked a visual renaissance in action films. This aesthetic DNA can be seen in **Extraction** (2020) and **Kate** (2021). The series also revitalized Keanu Reeves' career, similar to how **Taken** (2008) reinvented Liam Neeson as an action star, proving that older actors could carry physically demanding roles.

The Continental's elaborate criminal underworld, with its gold coins and strict rules, inspired a wave of films exploring hidden societies. **Hotel Artemis** (2018) directly borrowed the concept of a criminal safe haven, while **Gunpowder Milkshake** (2021) adopted similar assassin-culture worldbuilding. This approach to creating a rich mythology within the action genre traces back to **The Matrix** (1999), another Keanu Reeves vehicle that balanced complex world-building with spectacular action. sections.content: John Wick's fight scenes prioritize wide shots and longer takes, letting audiences fully appreciate the complexity of the choreography. This approach contrasts with the rapid-cut style of films like **Quantum of Solace** (2008). The franchise's success influenced films like **Mission: Impossible - Fallout** (2018) and **The Raid 2** (2014) to embrace more elaborate, clearly filmed combat sequences. The integration of firearms and martial arts created a distinctive fighting style that's both balletic and brutally efficient.
